learning_objective: 🎯 Level up your data skills! Learn how to clean messy data, calculate descriptive statistics, and read/write real-world CSV files.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: अल्पविराम से अलग किए गए मान

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Pandas can do math instantly! Functions like `max()`, `min()`, `sum()`, `mean()` (average), `median()` (middle value), and `mode()` (most frequent value) help summarize huge datasets in one line of code.
You can organize data easily. `sort_values(by='Column')` sorts the rows based on the data inside a specific column. `sort_index()` sorts the DataFrame based on its row labels.
This is filtering using True/False conditions. For example, `df[df['Marks'] > 90]` will check every row and return ONLY the rows where the student scored more than 90.
Real-world data is often incomplete, represented as NaN (Not a Number). You can either drop rows with missing data using `dropna()` or fill the empty spaces with a default value using `fillna(0)`.
CSV (Comma Separated Values) is the most common format for data. `pd.read_csv('file.csv')` imports the file into a DataFrame, and `df.to_csv('new_file.csv')` saves your DataFrame to your hard drive.

fun_activity.title: 🧹 The Data Cleaner
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine a dataset with a missing age: `[25, NaN, 22, 28]`. If you calculate the average without Pandas, it crashes. But Pandas is smart! It automatically ignores NaN values when calculating `.mean()`, keeping your program safe.

exam_tips: 📌 Axis is a crucial concept! `axis=0` means the operation runs vertically down the columns (default). `axis=1` means the operation runs horizontally across the rows.
📌 To sort in descending order, you must explicitly write: `df.sort_values(by='Column', ascending=False)`.
📌 Know the difference between `mean()` (average of all numbers) and `median()` (the exact middle number when sorted, which is better if there are extreme outliers).
quick_recap: ⭐ CSV files are essentially just plain text files where columns are separated by commas, making them lightweight and universal.
⭐ Boolean indexing works just like the WHERE clause in SQL databases.
⭐ `dropna()` deletes the entire row if even a single NaN value is present in it.
